title: An incentive-driven on-chain semi-asynchronous federated learning method

pse.problem: Existing federated learning methods lack economic incentives for data holders to participate actively, suffer from centralization vulnerabilities, and lack a robust defense against malicious participants.
pse.solution_function: The invention introduces an on-chain semi-asynchronous federated learning method that incentivizes participation using a blockchain-based reward system. Data holders perform local computations and upload the results to a decentralized network, allowing the global model to be updated iteratively without exposing original data. The system's control flow is managed by smart contracts, which enforce reward distribution based on contributions and monitor model training results for potential attacks.
pse.solution_structure: The solution consists of multiple data holders connected through a decentralized network, each with local data storage and computation capabilities. A blockchain serves as the backbone, hosting smart contracts that manage rewards, control data flow, and oversee the federated learning process. Participating nodes include a manager node and worker nodes.
pse.solution_implementation: In each round of iteration, the manager node initiates the training process by broadcasting the current global model to worker nodes. Each worker node performs local computations on its private data, updates the model parameters, and signs the results using its digital identity before submitting them back to the manager node. The manager node collects signed results from all worker nodes and aggregates them to update the global model. Smart contracts on the blockchain manage rewards, distributing incentives based on each node's contribution to the federated learning process. To combat malicious behavior, smart contracts also monitor the quality of submitted results and penalize nodes that provide incorrect or low-quality data.
pse.effect: The proposed solution addresses the identified limitations by enhancing collaboration through economic incentives, reducing centralization vulnerabilities by employing a decentralized network, and implementing robust defense mechanisms against malicious participants. The outcome is a more credible and efficient federated learning method that encourages active participation and ensures data privacy.
